caption: Figure 1: Coupled mechanisms of training degradation. Terminal supervision can yield negative aggregate tool credit. Token-mean aggregation can further amplify this signal by upweighting longer incorrect rollouts, while retries prolong these rollouts and extend negative credit to recovery attempts.

Figure 2: Training dynamics of MT-GRPO. (a) Validation accuracy peaks and then falls below the non-agentic reference. (b) Tool-execution success declines despite broadly stable tool-use rates. (c) Mean tool-call counts rise for incorrect trajectories and remain relatively stable for correct ones.

Figure 4: Length weighting and aggregate tool credit. (a) Token-mean aggregation shifts credit downward relative to trajectory-mean aggregation. (b) Length weighting turns positive tool credit negative in 73.6% of batches. This shifts the balance toward penalizing sampled tool calls.

Figure 5: Retry behavior and continuation length. (a) A tool call in the next turn is more likely after failed than successful executions. (b) First-execution failure is associated with longer subsequent generation. (c) Incorrect trajectories have higher retry rates across all four models on MATH.

Figure 6: Overview of TACA. TACA adjusts tool-call and decision-token advantages using within- prompt reward statistics from tool-using and direct-answer rollouts. These adjustments and replay supervision from correct trajectories jointly guide tool-use decisions and tool-call generation.

Figure 7: Training dynamics on Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct. (a) Both methods improve training accuracy. TACA maintains (b) substantial tool use, (c) a smaller share of no-tool failures, and (d) a higher logged execution-success metric. Appendix I.5 defines the metrics and smoothing.
Figure 8: Pooled reward means under trajectory and turn weighting. Incorrect trajectories contribute a larger share of generated turns than of sampled trajectories, lowering the turn-weighted mean.
